messages.subject: simsem and MG-CFA simulation
parts:
Hello!

I'm using the package simsem on a simulation study looking at measurement invariance for ordinal data.  I'm using the lavaan syntax specification and relying heavily on the following two vignettes provided on the simsem website:

https://github.com/simsem/simsem/blob/master/SupportingDocs/Examples/Version05/ex6/ex6.R

https://github.com/simsem/simsem/blob/master/SupportingDocs/Examples/Version05/exMultipleFormat/ordered.R

 I noticed with the multiple group syntax, there is an error when I run it. I changed the rep count to 100 instead of 1000 and group size from 200 to 100,  and there is an extra replication added, so instead of 100 reps, there are 101 reps. Here is the syntax:

library(simsem)

 # The simulateData function still has a bug in setting multiple-group parameters

# Thus, in this example, the population data of each group are created manually and are fed to the sim function.

 # a) Noninvariance

 popNoninvariance1 <- "

f1 =~ 0.7*y1 + 0.7*y2 + 0.7*y3 + 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6

f1 ~~ 1*f1

y1 ~~ 0.51*y1

y2 ~~ 0.51*y2

y3 ~~ 0.51*y3

y4 ~~ 0.51*y4

y5 ~~ 0.51*y5

y6 ~~ 0.51*y6

f1 ~ 0*1

y1 ~ -0.2*1

y2 ~ -0.1*1

y3 ~ 0*1

y4 ~ 0.1*1

y5 ~ 0.2*1

y6 ~ 0.3*1

"

 popNoninvariance2 <- "

f1 =~ 0.7*y1 + 0.7*y2 + 0.7*y3

f2 =~ 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6

f1 ~~ 1*f1

f2 ~~ 1*f2

f1 ~~ 0.5*f2

y1 ~~ 0.51*y1

y2 ~~ 0.51*y2

y3 ~~ 0.51*y3

y4 ~~ 0.51*y4

y5 ~~ 0.51*y5

y6 ~~ 0.51*y6

f1 ~ 0*1

f2 ~ 0*1

y1 ~ 0.2*1

y2 ~ 0.1*1

y3 ~ 0*1

y4 ~ -0.1*1

y5 ~ -0.2*1

y6 ~ -0.3*1

"

 

# Population data are created with 100 cases in each group

 popDataNoninvariance1 <- simulateData(popNoninvariance1, sample.nobs = 100)

popDataNoninvariance2 <- simulateData(popNoninvariance2, sample.nobs = 100)

popDataNoninvariance <- rbind(popDataNoninvariance1, popDataNoninvariance2)

popDataNoninvariance <- data.frame(popDataNoninvariance, group = rep(c(1, 2), each = 100))

 analyzeNoninvariance <- "

f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3

f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6

f1 ~~ 1*f1

f2 ~~ 1*f2

f1 ~~ c(1, NA)*f2

y1 ~~ y1

y2 ~~ y2

y3 ~~ y3

y4 ~~ y4

y5 ~~ y5

y6 ~~ y6

f1 ~ 0*1

f2 ~ 0*1

y1 ~ 1

y2 ~ 1

y3 ~ 1

y4 ~ 1

y5 ~ 1

y6 ~ 1

"

 outNoninvariance <- lavaan(analyzeNoninvariance, data = popDataNoninvariance, group = "group")

Output.a <- sim(100, analyzeNoninvariance, n=list(200, 200), rawData = popDataNoninvariance, group = "group", std.lv = TRUE, lavaanfun = "lavaan")

# Output.a <- sim(100, list(model = analyzeNoninvariance, group = "group", std.lv = TRUE), n=list(100, 100), rawData = popDataNoninvariance)

getCutoff(Output.a, 0.05)

plotCutoff(Output.a, 0.05)

summary(Output.a)

I'm not sure why an extra replication is added, no matter how I change the model and rep counts. 

Additionally, I'm having some issues when I try to simulate ordinal data for multiple groups. Here is a simple example of my code:

set.seed(12345)

popModel1 <- "

#latent variable definition

f1 =~ 0.6*y1 + 0.5*y2 + 0.4*y3 + 0.3*y4

#scaling factors

y1 ~*~ 1*y1

y2 ~*~ 1*y2

y3 ~*~ 1*y3

y4 ~*~ 1*y4

#(co)variances

f1 ~~ 1*f1

#thresholds

y1 | 0.5*t1 + 0.7*t2

y2 | 0.25*t1 + 0.5*t2

y3 | 0*t1 + 0.1*t2

y4 | -0.5*t1 + -0.25*t2

"

 popModel2 <- "

#latent variable definition

f1 =~ 0.6*y1 + 0.5*y2 + 0.4*y3 + 0.3*y4

#scaling factors

y1 ~*~ 1*y1

y2 ~*~ 1*y2

y3 ~*~ 1*y3

y4 ~*~ 1*y4

#(co)variances

f1 ~~ 1*f1

#thresholds

y1 | 0.5*t1 + 0.7*t2

y2 | 0.25*t1 + 0.5*t2

y3 | 0*t1 + 0.1*t2

y4 | -0.5*t1 + -0.25*t2

"

# Population data are created with 500 cases in each group

 popModel1 <- simulateData(popModel1, sample.nobs = 500)

popModel2 <- simulateData(popModel2, sample.nobs = 500)

popModelC <- rbind(popModel1, popModel2)

popModelC <- data.frame(popModelC, group = rep(c(1, 2), each = 500))

 

head(popModelC)

summary(popModelC)

 

analyzeModel <- "

f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4

y1 ~*~ 1*y1

y2 ~*~ 1*y2

y3 ~*~ 1*y3

y4 ~*~ 1*y4

"

Output <- sim(100, analyzeModel, n = list(500, 500), rawData=popModelC, group="group", std.lv=TRUE, lavaanfun="cfa", ordered = c("y1", "y2", "y3", "y4"))

When I run the code, I get 101 reps again and the following error: 

Error in lav_options_set(opt) : 

lavaan ERROR: missing="fiml" not available in the categorical setting.


I'm not sure what needs to be changed to successfully simulate two groups with ordinal data and analyze the output. 

Is there some bug fix for this, or am I missing some piece of code to successfully run the simulations for multiple groups?

Thanks,

-Gina

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: simsem and MG-CFA simulation
parts: I'm using the package simsem on a simulation study looking at measurement invariance for ordinal data

I don't know what causes that weird issue, but my advice would be to NOT use simsem.  It is not set up for model comparison, although they wrote an anova() method that applies in the simple case of normal data.  Your code is already generating data directly from population-model syntax.  Instead of treating that as rawData= in sim() (which was only designed to generate continuous data with the same skew/kurtosis, so you will NOT get categorical data that way), you should just analyze the generated data with lavaan.  You can write a function that does the data generation, then pass that to lavaanList().  You can write another function (for the FUN= argument) to collect the output you want, including using update() to fit a more constrained invariance model.

Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
